newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania Ion Tiriac bank gets $40 mln loan.
newsitem.headline: Romania Ion Tiriac bank gets $40 mln loan.

text.p: Romanian private bank Banca Ion Tiriac SA signed on Friday a $40 million two-year syndicated loan arranged by London Forfaiting Asia Ltd.
Lead managers of the loan, which involves another 13 foreign banks as managers and participants, are Credit Suisse First Boston and Landesbank Schleswig-Holstein Girozentrale.
The two-year loan bears an interest rate based on the six-month LIBOR with a 175 basis points margin, bank president Constantin Duna told a news conference.
Duna said the initial loan request for $25 million rose to $40 million thanks to strong interest during subscription.
"The loan will help develop the bank's general activity," Duna said.
He said the bank was also planning other raisings from the international capital markets and was seeking a strategic foreign partner to increase the bank's equity capital.
"This will allow us to expand and offer greater support to private companies in the industrial, agricultural and services sectors," Duna said.

Ion Tiriac bank was the first private commercial bank opened in Romania after the 1989 fall of communism. It was founded by Ion Tiriac, a Romanian former tennis star who once managed Boris Becker, and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development holds 20 percent of the bank's capital.
